notes: This contract maps a later-arriving equal-time timestamped interaction under Time Advance Request Available to the pinned 2025 service semantics. The producer first advances to 4 with lookahead 1 and no pending TSO; the recipient's TARA(5) grants at 5. Only then does the producer send TSO(5) and advance to 5. The recipient issues TARA(6), and the later equal-time receiveInteraction follows the first grant and precedes the second available grant at time 5. This is distinct from an equal-time TSO already queued at the RTI when the first TARA is requested, which §8.9 requires before that grant and is covered by a separate implementation-profile case. It does not generalize this result to TAR, NMR, NMRA, or Flush Queue Request, and it is not Requirements Lab validation or conformance evidence.

tests: cpp/tests/timestamped_send_interaction_retraction_catch2.cpp::Embedded TARA delivers a queued equal-time TSO before its grant
requirements.notes: The portable Java and C++ TCK parity cases first grant TARA(5) with no pending interaction, then send TSO(5), advance the producer to 5, and request TARA(6); they verify receiveInteraction at 5 follows the initial grant and precedes the second grant at 5. They do not claim the already-queued-equality before-grant rule. The Catch2 reference is a separate HLA_EVOKED implementation-profile case that explicitly queues an equal-time TSO before TARA and verifies it precedes the grant; it is not conformance evidence. RL-313/RL-316 record clipped Lab candidate exports; full clause 8.9 controls the before-grant set and permits later equal-time arrivals after grant.
